title: Atom Builder
subject: Chemistry
summary: Build atoms and ions particle by particle on the bench, then check your model.

intro.text: Welcome to Atom Builder. Add particles to build each atom or ion, then check your model. You can follow the captions with sound off.

invalid.text: That spot does not work for this particle or shell. Check the feedback and try another position.

missions.title: Build carbon-12
missions.goalText: Build a neutral carbon atom with 6 protons, 6 neutrons, and 6 electrons.
hints: Carbon is C. Set 6 protons and 6 neutrons.
Carbon-12 needs 6 protons and 6 neutrons. Neutral means 6 electrons too.

start.text: Build carbon-12. Start with six protons and six neutrons. Add six electrons too, because the atom is neutral.

complete.text: Carbon-12 is ready: six protons, six neutrons, and six electrons. Continue to the questions when you are ready.

questions.prompt: In the carbon-12 build, how many protons should the atom have?
questions.explanation: Carbon-12 has 6 protons. You may have mixed up the mass number 12 with the proton count, or swapped protons and neutrons.

questions.prompt: A neutral carbon-12 atom has 6 protons. How many electrons does it have?
questions.explanation: A neutral carbon-12 atom has 6 electrons. You may have used the mass number or neutron count instead of matching the electron count to the proton count.

missions.title: Make Na+
missions.goalText: Build Na+ with 11 protons, 12 neutrons, 10 electrons, and configuration 2,8.
hints: Check what Na+ says about charge.
Sodium has 11 protons; +1 means one fewer electron.
Use 11 protons, 12 neutrons, and 10 electrons. Those electrons fill 2,8.

start.text: Now make Na+. Sodium has eleven protons. A +1 charge means it has lost one electron.

complete.text: Na+ has eleven protons, twelve neutrons, and ten electrons. Its electron configuration is two, eight.

questions.prompt: The Na+ build has 11 protons. How many electrons should it have?
questions.explanation: Na+ has 10 electrons. You may have treated +1 as one electron, or kept the 11 electrons of a neutral atom; here the positive charge means one fewer electron than protons.

questions.prompt: Which electron configuration matches the Na+ build?
questions.explanation: The Na+ build has configuration 2,8. You may have used the proton count to add a third-shell electron, instead of accounting for the +1 charge and 10 electrons.

missions.title: Build carbon-14
missions.goalText: Build carbon-14 with 6 protons, 8 neutrons, 6 electrons, and charge 0.
hints: Compare the mass number with the proton count.
Carbon has 6 protons. Use mass number 14 to find its neutrons.

start.text: Build C-14. It has six protons. Compare mass number fourteen with the proton count to find its neutrons.

complete.text: C-14 has six protons, eight neutrons, and six electrons. Its charge is zero.

questions.prompt: Carbon-14 has a mass number of 14 and 6 protons. How many neutrons does it have?
questions.explanation: Carbon-14 has 8 neutrons. You may have mistaken the mass number 14 for the neutron count, or carried over carbon-12's 6 neutrons.

questions.prompt: The carbon-14 build has charge 0 and 6 protons. How many electrons should it have?
questions.explanation: With charge 0, this carbon-14 build has 6 electrons. You may have used the mass number or neutron count instead of matching electrons to protons for a neutral atom.

missions.title: Make Cl-
missions.goalText: Build Cl- with 17 protons, 18 neutrons, 18 electrons, and a complete outer shell.
hints: A negative charge means an extra electron.
Chlorine has 17 protons; add one electron for -1.
Use 17 protons, 18 neutrons, and 18 electrons. Shells 2,8,8 make a complete outer shell.

start.text: Make Cl-. Chlorine has seventeen protons. A negative charge means one extra electron.

complete.text: Cl- has seventeen protons, eighteen neutrons, and electron configuration two, eight, eight, with a complete outer shell.

questions.prompt: The Cl- build has 17 protons. How many electrons should it have?
questions.explanation: Cl- has 18 electrons. You may have confused the 17 protons with the electron count; the -1 charge means one extra electron.

questions.prompt: Which description matches the Cl- build?
questions.explanation: Cl- has configuration 2,8,8 and a complete outer shell. You may have stopped at 17 electrons or counted the total without checking how the electrons are arranged in shells.
